teile.einleitung: Swiss Re is one of the largest reinsurance companies in the world and is based in Zurich. A reinsurer does not insure individual people, but other insurance companies. Swiss Re was founded after the devastating fire of Glarus in 1861.
wichtigste: Swiss Re is a reinsurer based in Zurich.
A reinsurer insures other insurance companies.
The fire of Glarus in 1861 led to the founding of Swiss Re.
The company was founded in 1863.
Swiss Re is one of the two largest reinsurers in the world.
Swiss Re helps to bear the costs of large disasters.

abschnitte.text: During the night of 10 to 11 May 1861, a fire broke out in **Glarus**. A strong Föhn wind drove the flames through the town, and about two thirds of it burned down. Around 2000 people lost their homes. The Swiss insurance companies could hardly pay for the huge damage.

After this disaster it became clear that insurance companies themselves need protection. That is why in 1863 the insurer Helvetia, the Schweizerische Kreditanstalt and the Basler Handelsbank founded the **Swiss Reinsurance Company** (Schweizerische Rückversicherungs-Gesellschaft). Its headquarters was in **Zurich**, where it still stands today at Mythenquai on Lake Zurich. Later the name became Swiss Re.

An insurance company collects money from many customers. But after a very large loss, for example after an **earthquake** or a storm, it would have to pay huge sums all at once. That is why it passes part of the risk on to a **reinsurer** and pays it a premium for this. A reinsurer spreads risks from all over the world so that it can bear even large disasters.

Swiss Re employs many experts who study **natural disasters**, diseases and other risks. They calculate, for example, how often strong storms or floods occur. The studies in the sigma series about insurance and disasters are well known. **Climate change** is also an important subject for reinsurers, because severe weather may become more frequent.

Swiss Re has offices in many countries on all continents. Besides reinsurance, it also offers insurance directly to companies. The company is listed on the Swiss stock exchange. Its biggest competitor is Munich Re from Germany.

begriffe.erklaerung: Insurance for insurance companies.
The amount you pay for an insurance policy.
The possibility that damage will happen.
A warm, dry wind that blows down the slopes in the Alps.

gewusst: The famous London skyscraper 30 St Mary Axe, called “the Gherkin” because of its shape, was built for Swiss Re.
After the fire, Glarus was rebuilt with wide, straight streets so that a fire could not spread so quickly again.
After large disasters such as hurricanes, reinsurers often pay out billions.

teile.einleitung: The Zurich Cantonal Bank, ZKB for short, is the bank of the canton of Zurich. It belongs to the canton and is the largest of the Swiss cantonal banks. Because the canton is liable for its debts through the state guarantee, it is considered a particularly safe bank.
wichtigste: The Zurich Cantonal Bank belongs to the canton of Zurich.
The state guarantee means that the canton is liable for the bank’s debts.
Banks that belong to a canton are called cantonal banks.
The ZKB was founded in 1870.
It is the largest cantonal bank in Switzerland.
It pays part of its profit to the canton and the municipalities.
Its headquarters is on Bahnhofstrasse in Zurich.

abschnitte.text: The Zurich Cantonal Bank was founded in 1870. At that time farmers, craftsmen and small tradespeople found it hard to get loans from the large private banks. The **cantonal bank** was therefore meant to serve the whole population. From the very beginning its task was to promote the economy in the canton of Zurich.

The ZKB has a **state guarantee**. This means that if the bank could no longer pay its debts, the canton of Zurich would have to step in. That is why many people trust the ZKB with their savings. In return the bank pays the canton a **compensation payment** for this security.

There are 24 **cantonal banks** in Switzerland; almost every canton has one. Examples are the Bern Cantonal Bank, the Lucerne Cantonal Bank and the Banque Cantonale Vaudoise. Most have a state guarantee, but not all of them. Together the cantonal banks are among the most important banks in the country.

The ZKB is an independent **public-law institution** of the canton. Its highest body is the bank council, which is elected by the Zurich cantonal parliament (Kantonsrat). The cantonal parliament also supervises the bank. Because the ZKB is so large, it has been considered **systemically important** since 2013.

The ZKB has branches in many municipalities in the canton of Zurich. It offers accounts for children and young people, mortgages and advice for companies. Every year hundreds of millions of francs of its profit flow to the **canton** and the municipalities. The bank also supports cultural, sports and nature projects in the region.

begriffe.erklaerung: A bank that belongs to a canton or is controlled by it.
The canton’s promise to pay the bank’s debts if necessary.
The parliament of the canton of Zurich.
The money left over when costs are subtracted from income.

gewusst: The Zurich Cantonal Bank is larger than some well-known private banks in Switzerland.
The ZKB’s profit indirectly helps to pay for schools, roads and other tasks of the canton.
Not only people from Zurich, but anyone can open an account with the ZKB.

teile.einleitung: The Swatch Group is the largest watch group in the world and is based in Biel in the canton of Bern. It includes famous brands such as Omega, Longines, Tissot and of course Swatch. In the 1980s the colourful plastic Swatch watch helped to rescue the Swiss watch industry from a severe crisis.
wichtigste: The Swatch Group is the largest watchmaker in the world.
Its headquarters is in Biel/Bienne.
The first Swatch watch of 1983 was made of plastic.
The quartz crisis was a crisis in the Swiss watch industry caused by cheap quartz watches from Asia.
Nicolas G. Hayek ran the group for a long time and is considered the saviour of the watch industry.
The group includes brands such as Omega, Longines, Tissot, Rado and Breguet.
The company ETA makes watch movements for many brands.

abschnitte.text: In the 1970s cheap **quartz watches** from Japan and other Asian countries came onto the market. They were very accurate and cost little. Swiss watch companies, on the other hand, were still mainly building expensive mechanical watches. In this **quartz crisis**, tens of thousands of people in the Swiss watch industry lost their jobs.

Two large watch groups, ASUAG and SSIH, were in deep trouble. The management consultant **Nicolas G. Hayek** helped to merge them in 1983. This created SMH, which was renamed **Swatch Group** in 1998. Hayek ran the company for many years, and since 2003 his son Nick Hayek has led the group.

In 1983 the first **Swatch** came onto the market. It was made of plastic and had only 51 parts, far fewer than other watches. This meant it could be made cheaply and in large numbers. With bright colours and ever new designs, the Swatch became a **fashion item** that many people collected.

The Swatch Group includes luxury brands such as **Omega**, Breguet and Blancpain. There are also brands such as Longines, Rado, Tissot, Certina, Mido and Hamilton. Omega is the official **timekeeper** of the Olympic Games. An Omega Speedmaster was there at the first Moon landing in 1969.

An important part of the group is the company **ETA** in Grenchen. It makes watch movements, the inner workings of watches. For a long time ETA also supplied such movements to many other Swiss watch companies. The Swatch Group employs tens of thousands of people, mainly in the **Jura arc** between Geneva and Schaffhausen.

begriffe.erklaerung: A watch in which a tiny vibrating quartz crystal keeps the beat.
A watch that runs with a spring and gearwheels, without a battery.
The inner workings of a watch, which drive the hands.
The one who measures times exactly at sporting events.

gewusst: The name Swatch is often explained as short for “Second Watch”.
Nicolas G. Hayek was also involved in developing the Smart small car.
At the Olympic Games, Omega measures times accurately to a thousandth of a second.

teile.einleitung: Sunrise is a Swiss telecommunications company for mobile phones, internet and television. After Swisscom, it is the second-largest provider in Switzerland. In 2021 Sunrise merged with the cable network operator UPC.
wichtigste: Sunrise offers mobile phone services, internet, landline and television.
Sunrise’s biggest competitor is Swisscom.
In 2021 Sunrise merged with UPC.
Its headquarters is in Opfikon near Zurich.
Sunrise runs its own mobile network with 5G.
Since 2024 Sunrise has been listed on the Swiss stock exchange again.

abschnitte.text: Sunrise sells **mobile phone contracts**, internet connections, landline telephony and television. For this the company runs its own **mobile network** with thousands of aerials all over Switzerland. Internet and television come directly into homes via the cable network. Sunrise also owns cheaper brands such as yallo.

After the end of the state monopoly in the 1990s, other companies besides Swisscom were allowed to offer telephone services. Sunrise came about at this time and grew in 2001 through a merger with the provider **diAx**. For a long time Sunrise belonged to foreign investors. In 2020 the American group **Liberty Global** bought the company.

In Switzerland Liberty Global already owned **UPC**, the largest cable network in the country. In 2021 Sunrise and UPC were combined into one company. This created a strong competitor for Swisscom, offering mobile and cable network services from one source. The UPC brand later disappeared, and today everything is called Sunrise.

There are three large mobile companies on the Swiss market: **Swisscom**, Sunrise and Salt. They all build their own networks and compete for customers with offers and prices. This **competition** means that there are many different contracts. In tests by specialist magazines, Swiss mobile networks usually do very well compared with other countries.

Before taking out a mobile phone contract, you should compare how much data you really need. The **contract length** is also important, because some contracts run for one or two years. Abroad, **roaming** can become expensive if it is not included in the contract. There are special contracts with cost control for children and young people.

begriffe.erklaerung: Sending speech, texts and data over networks, for example by mobile phone.
A network of aerials through which mobile phones make calls and go online.
Using your mobile phone on the network of a foreign provider.
When only one single company is allowed to offer something.

gewusst: Before the market was opened up, only the state-owned PTT was allowed to offer telephone connections in Switzerland.
Sunrise was one of the first providers in Europe to put a 5G network into operation.
In its history the company has been on the stock exchange several times, disappeared from it and come back again.

teile.einleitung: Stadler Rail is a Swiss company that builds trains and trams. Its headquarters is in Bussnang in the canton of Thurgau. One well-known example is the Giruno, a high-speed train that runs through the Gotthard Base Tunnel for SBB.
wichtigste: Stadler Rail builds trains, trams and rack railways.
Its headquarters is in Bussnang TG.
The Giruno runs through the Gotthard Base Tunnel.
The company was founded in 1942 by Ernst Stadler.
Peter Spuhler took over the small company in 1989 and made it big.
Stadler supplies vehicles to many countries around the world.

abschnitte.titel: From small business to global group
abschnitte.text: In 1942 **Ernst Stadler** founded an engineering office in Zurich and soon built small locomotives. Later the company moved to **Bussnang** in Thurgau. In 1989 **Peter Spuhler** bought the business, which at the time had only around 18 employees. Today about 14,000 people work for Stadler (as of 2024).

The **Giruno** is a high-speed train that Stadler built for SBB. It is around 200 metres long and can travel at up to 250 kilometres an hour. Since 2019 it has run through the **Gotthard Base Tunnel** and on to Italy. The name comes from Romansh and means buzzard.

The **FLIRT**, a regional train that runs in many European countries, is very successful. The KISS is a double-decker train that runs, for example, on the Zurich S-Bahn network. Stadler also builds **trams**, for example for cities in Switzerland, Germany and Norway. There are also rack railways for steep mountain routes and vehicles for narrow-gauge railways.

Stadler has works in Switzerland, Germany, Poland, Hungary, Spain, the USA and other countries. The company supplies trains to many countries, from Europe to North Africa and North America. In the USA, for example, electric double-decker trains from Stadler run in California. Since 2019 Stadler has been listed on the Swiss **stock exchange**.

abschnitte.titel: Trains with new kinds of drive
abschnitte.text: Not all lines have overhead wires for electricity. That is why Stadler also builds trains with **batteries** or with hydrogen. Such trains run without a diesel engine and give off no exhaust fumes while running. In this way the railway industry helps to protect the climate.

begriffe.erklaerung: A train that can travel faster than 200 kilometres an hour.
A train with two levels, one above the other.
A railway with a cogwheel that grips a toothed rail so that it can climb steep mountains.
The power line above the tracks from which electric trains get their electricity.

gewusst: Stadler also built the new vehicles for the Pilatus Railway, the steepest rack railway in the world.
When Peter Spuhler took it over in 1989, Stadler had fewer than 20 employees; today it has thousands.
In Bussnang the trains are tried out on the company’s own test track before they are delivered.

teile.einleitung: Swisscom is the largest telecommunications company in Switzerland. It offers mobile phone contracts, internet, television and many IT services. Swisscom grew out of the former PTT, and the majority of the company still belongs to the Confederation today.
wichtigste: Swisscom is the largest telecoms provider in Switzerland.
The majority of Swisscom belongs to the Confederation.
Swisscom grew out of the state-owned PTT.
Its headquarters is in Ittigen near Bern.
Swisscom has been listed on the stock exchange since 1998.
Swisscom owns the company Fastweb in Italy.

abschnitte.text: In the past the **PTT** was responsible for post, telephone and telegraph in Switzerland. It was a state enterprise and had a **monopoly** on telephones. In 1998 the PTT was split up: the Post became a separate company, and the telephone part became Swisscom. In the same year Swisscom shares were listed on the stock exchange.

The **Confederation** owns a little more than half of Swisscom’s shares. This is laid down by law. The state wants to make sure that the important infrastructure for telephone and internet stays in Swiss hands. Swisscom must also guarantee the **universal service**, that is, telephone and internet for all households, even in remote mountain valleys.

Swisscom runs a large **mobile network** with 5G and a fibre-optic network for fast internet. With its blue service it sells television, films and sports broadcasts. For companies, Swisscom offers data centres, cloud services and IT security. The company employs many thousands of people in Switzerland and trains numerous apprentices.

In 2007 Swisscom bought the Italian telecoms company **Fastweb**. At the end of 2024 it also took over Vodafone Italia. This makes Swisscom one of the big providers in Italy too. These purchases cost many billions of francs.

In Switzerland many people still call a mobile phone a **Natel** today. The name comes from the National Car Telephone (Nationales Autotelefon), which the PTT offered from 1978. The first car phones were heavy, expensive and only built into cars. Today most people go online with their **smartphone** on the Swisscom network or with its competitors Sunrise and Salt.

begriffe.erklaerung: The former state enterprise for post, telephone and telegraph.
Important services that must be offered to everyone throughout the country.
A thin glass cable that transmits data very quickly using light.
A part of a company that you can buy and sell.

gewusst: The word Natel is used almost only in Switzerland and comes from the time of the PTT.
Swisscom runs thousands of aerials in Switzerland, including on high mountains.
The PTT used to put up public telephone boxes all over Switzerland; today almost all of them have disappeared.

teile.einleitung: Swiss International Air Lines, Swiss for short, is the largest airline in Switzerland. Its aircraft carry the Swiss cross on the tail. Swiss was created in 2002 after the former airline Swissair had to stop all its flights in 2001.
wichtigste: Swiss is the national airline of Switzerland.
The Swiss cross can be seen on the tail of the aircraft.
Its predecessor Swissair had to stop all its flights in 2001.
Swiss was created in 2002 from the regional airline Crossair.
Its most important hub is Zurich Airport.
Since 2005 Swiss has belonged to the German Lufthansa Group.
Swiss is a member of Star Alliance.

abschnitte.text: **Swissair** was founded in 1931 and was the pride of Switzerland for decades. At the end of the 1990s it bought stakes in many other airlines and made huge losses. On 2 October 2001 the money ran out, and the aircraft stayed on the ground. This **grounding** shocked the whole country, and thousands of passengers were stranded.

The new Swiss was created from the regional airline **Crossair** and parts of Swissair. The Confederation, the cantons and companies gave a lot of money for this. On 31 March 2002 Swiss began flying. The first years were difficult, because the company made losses.

In 2005 the German **Lufthansa** took over Swiss. But Swiss remained a separate airline with a Swiss name and the Swiss cross. Its official headquarters is in **Basel**, but most flights take off from Zurich and Geneva. The group also includes the holiday airline Edelweiss.

Swiss flies to many destinations in Europe, America, Africa and Asia. For long-haul routes it uses large aircraft such as the **Boeing 777** and the Airbus A330. In Europe it often flies the **Airbus A220**, formerly called the CSeries. In 2016 Swiss was the first airline in the world to use this aircraft.

On board, passengers traditionally get a piece of **Swiss chocolate**. The on-board kitchen often serves dishes from different Swiss regions. Announcements are usually made in German, French and English. The red tail with the white cross makes the aircraft easy to recognise at airports all over the world.

begriffe.erklaerung: A company that transports people and goods by aeroplane.
When all the aircraft of an airline have to stay on the ground.
An airport where many flights come together and passengers change planes.
An alliance of airlines that work together.

gewusst: Every year Swiss hands out millions of small chocolates to its passengers.
Because of its reliability and its wealth, Swissair was long known as the “flying bank”.
The Airbus A220 was developed in Canada, and Swiss was its first customer.

teile.einleitung: Volg is a chain of small grocery shops found mainly in villages. The red shops with the slogan “frisch und fründlich” make sure that people in the countryside can also shop close to home. Volg belongs to fenaco, a large agricultural cooperative.
wichtigste: Volg shops are found mainly in villages.
Volg belongs to the fenaco cooperative.
The name comes from an association of agricultural cooperatives in eastern Switzerland.
It is based in Winterthur.
There are about 600 Volg shops in Switzerland (as of 2024).
The well-known slogan is “frisch und fründlich”.

abschnitte.text: Volg shops are usually small and stand in the middle of the **village**. There you can get bread, milk, vegetables, meat and many other everyday things. Without Volg, many people in the countryside would have to travel to the next larger town. The village shop is especially important for older people without a car.

The name Volg comes from the **Association of Eastern Swiss Agricultural Cooperatives** (Verband ostschweizerischer landwirtschaftlicher Genossenschaften), founded in Winterthur in 1886. It supplied farmers with seed, feed and fertiliser. Shops also came about in the villages that sold food too. In 1993 the association joined with others to form **fenaco**.

**fenaco** is a cooperative that belongs to Switzerland’s agricultural cooperatives. Besides Volg, it also includes the Landi shops and many businesses that process food. It buys, for example, grain, potatoes and fruit from Swiss farms. In this way many regional products end up directly on the Volg shelves.

Many Volg shops sell products from their own village or the region. These can be eggs, cheese, honey or bread from the bakery next door. Under the brand **“Feins vom Dorf”** (fine things from the village), Volg offers specialities from small businesses. In this way the shops support farmers and craftspeople from the area.

Volg’s red lettering is known everywhere in the countryside. The slogan **“frisch und fründlich”** is in Swiss German dialect and means fresh and friendly. There are Volg shops in German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland, and some are run by independent shopkeepers. Some Volg shops have long opening hours or a **post office counter** in the shop.

begriffe.erklaerung: A business that belongs to its members.
Selling goods directly to customers in shops.
From the nearby area.
Providing the most important things you need to live.

gewusst: In many villages, Volg is the last shop after other shops have closed.
The Landi shops, which sell garden tools and animal feed, belong to fenaco just like Volg.
In some Volg shops you can also post parcels and buy stamps.

teile.einleitung: Victorinox is the company that makes the famous red Swiss pocket knife. It is based in Ibach in the canton of Schwyz and was founded in 1884 by Karl Elsener. The name Victorinox is made up of the first name Victoria and the word “inox” for stainless steel.
wichtigste: Victorinox makes the classic red Swiss pocket knife.
The name comes from Victoria and “inox” for stainless steel.
The company was founded in 1884 by Karl Elsener.
It is based in Ibach in the canton of Schwyz.
Since 1891 the company has supplied knives to the Swiss Army.
In 2005 Victorinox took over its competitor Wenger.
Today Victorinox also sells kitchen knives, watches and luggage.

abschnitte.text: In 1884 the cutler **Karl Elsener** opened a workshop in **Ibach** near Schwyz. He wanted the Swiss Army to stop buying its soldiers’ knives from Germany. In 1891 he supplied the first soldiers’ knives to the army. In 1897 he had the lighter **officer’s knife** with more tools protected by law.

When Karl Elsener’s mother **Victoria** died in 1909, he named the company after her. From the 1920s stainless steel was used, in French “acier inoxydable”, **inox** for short. Victoria and inox gave the name **Victorinox**. The company emblem is a Swiss cross in a shield.

The classic Swiss pocket knife has red handles with the **Swiss cross**. Depending on the model, it contains blades, scissors, a saw, a tin opener, a screwdriver, tweezers and a toothpick. The Swiss Champ model has over 30 functions. After the Second World War, American soldiers called the knife the **Swiss Army Knife**, and that is how it became known worldwide.

For a long time there were two makers of Swiss Army knives: Victorinox in German-speaking Switzerland and **Wenger** in Delémont in the Jura. The army divided its orders between the two. In 2005 Victorinox took over the company Wenger. Today the knives are sold under the name Victorinox.

All over the world, the pocket knife is considered typically Swiss, like chocolate and cheese. Victorinox produces tens of thousands of knives every day, most of them in Ibach. Astronauts have also taken Swiss pocket knives with them on space missions. Victorinox is a **family business** and belongs to a foundation of the Elsener family.

begriffe.erklaerung: A small knife whose blades and tools can be folded away.
Steel that does not rust because chromium is mixed in, also called inox.
A craftsman who makes knives.
A tool that combines many different tools in one.

gewusst: A Swiss pocket knife is in the collection of the Museum of Modern Art in New York, because it is considered an example of good design.
In Brunnen on Lake Lucerne there is a Victorinox shop where you can assemble your own knife.
Pocket knives may not be taken onto an aeroplane in hand luggage, which is why Victorinox sold far fewer knives at airports after 2001.

teile.einleitung: Zweifel is the best-known crisps brand in Switzerland and is based in Spreitenbach in the canton of Aargau. The crunchy crisps are made from Swiss potatoes. More than half of all the crisps sold in Switzerland come from Zweifel.
wichtigste: Zweifel crisps are made from potatoes.
Zweifel has over 50 per cent of the Swiss crisps market.
The Zweifel crisps brand has existed since 1958.
The company has belonged to the Zweifel family since its beginnings.
The main factory is in Spreitenbach in the canton of Aargau.
Almost all the potatoes come from Swiss farmers.
The Zweifel family used to make Most, that is, fruit juice.

abschnitte.text: In 1898 the Zweifel family founded a company in Zurich-Höngg that made fruit juice, called **Most**. In the early 1950s a relative, Hans Meier, fried crisps in a large pan on his farm. The family took over this business, and in **1958** the Zweifel crisps brand came onto the market. In 1970 the large factory in **Spreitenbach** opened.

First the potatoes are washed and peeled. Then a machine cuts them into wafer-thin slices. These slices are **fried** in hot oil until they are crunchy. Since 2017 Zweifel has used **rapeseed oil** instead of sunflower oil. Finally the crisps are seasoned, for example with salt or paprika, and packed into bags.

Every year Zweifel processes about 25,000 tonnes of **potatoes**. Almost all of them come from over 250 farming families in Switzerland who grow them especially for Zweifel. Crisps need special potato varieties with little sugar so that they do not go too dark when fried. Only if the harvest is too small are potatoes from abroad sometimes used.

In Switzerland, Zweifel is the clear **market leader** for crisps and snacks. More than half of all crisps sold come from this company. Every year over 10,000 tonnes of crisps and snacks are made in Spreitenbach. The company employs over 500 people and is run by the third generation of the family.

The Zweifel group also includes a wine merchant, Zweifel 1898 AG in Zurich-Höngg. It sells wines and also produces its own wine. In 2022 Zweifel also took over a bakery company for baked goods. Zweifel is also known for its advertising, for example on the internet. When unwanted advertising pops up in a window there, you can usually close it with the small **X**.

begriffe.erklaerung: What percentage of all sales of a product comes from one company.
Cooking food by letting it swim in hot oil.
A company that belongs to a family and is run by it.
Juice from pressed apples or pears.

gewusst: About 25,000 tonnes of potatoes a year make only just over 10,000 tonnes of crisps and snacks, because a lot of water evaporates during frying.
After the Second World War, the family’s cider press was considered one of the most modern businesses in Europe.
The very first Zweifel crisps were still fried in a field pan on a farm.

teile.einleitung: Swiss Life is the largest life insurance company in Switzerland. The company helps people to save money for old age and to protect their families. Many people also know the name from ice hockey: the ZSC Lions play in the Swiss Life Arena in Zurich.
wichtigste: Swiss Life deals mainly with life insurance and retirement provision.
The company was founded in Zurich in 1857.
It used to be called the Swiss Pension Institution (Schweizerische Rentenanstalt).
Swiss Life also operates in France and Germany.
The company owns a great deal of property.
The ZSC Lions’ ice hockey stadium is called the Swiss Life Arena.

abschnitte.text: In 1857 **Conrad Widmer** founded the Schweizerische Rentenanstalt in Zurich. It was Switzerland’s first life insurance company. The idea: many people pay in small amounts regularly, and later **pensions** or payments to surviving dependants are paid out of this. Since 2004 the company has used the name Swiss Life.

**Life insurance** pays out money when the insured person dies or reaches a certain age. This means, for example, that the family is protected if a parent dies early. Many people also use such insurance to save for old age. Swiss Life also offers insurance against **disability**, that is, when someone can no longer work because of illness or an accident.

Switzerland has a **three-pillar system** for retirement provision. The first pillar is the state AVS, the second is occupational pension provision through the employer, and the third is voluntary saving. Swiss Life is especially important in the second pillar. Many companies insure their employees through Swiss Life or its foundations.

Insurance companies must invest the money paid in safely. Swiss Life invests a large part of it in **property**, that is, flats, office buildings and shops. It is one of the largest private property owners in Switzerland. With the rental income it can later pay the pensions.

Since 2022 the **ZSC Lions** have played in a new stadium in Zurich-Altstetten. Swiss Life bought the naming rights, which is why it is called the Swiss Life Arena. The stadium holds around 12,000 spectators. This **sponsorship** makes the company’s name known to many sports fans.

begriffe.erklaerung: Insurance that pays out money on death or when a certain age is reached.
Regular money you receive in old age when you no longer work.
Everything you do to have enough money to live on in old age.
The purchased right to give a stadium or event a name.

gewusst: Swiss Life is older than the Swiss federal state in its present constitution of 1874.
Before the Swiss Life Arena, the ZSC Lions played for decades in the Hallenstadion in Zurich-Oerlikon.
Swiss Life is one of the companies in the Swiss Market Index, Switzerland’s most important share index.

teile.einleitung: UBS is the largest bank in Switzerland and one of the most important banks in the world. It has its headquarters in two cities, Zurich and Basel. In 2023 UBS took over its former competitor Credit Suisse.
wichtigste: UBS is the largest bank in Switzerland.
It has its headquarters in Zurich and Basel.
In 2023 UBS took over Credit Suisse.
Today’s UBS was formed in 1998 from two large Swiss banks.
UBS is especially strong in wealth management.
Its logo shows three keys.
In the financial crisis of 2008, UBS needed help from the state.

abschnitte.text: Today’s UBS was formed in 1998 from the merger of the **Union Bank of Switzerland** (Schweizerische Bankgesellschaft) with the **Swiss Bank Corporation** (Schweizerischer Bankverein). The Union Bank came from Zurich and Winterthur, the Bank Corporation from Basel. That is why UBS still has two headquarters today. The logo with the three keys comes from the Bank Corporation and stands for trust, security and discretion.

UBS manages large amounts of **wealth** for rich people and companies all over the world. In this field it is one of the largest banks in the world. In Switzerland it also has many ordinary customers with accounts, cards and mortgages. It also advises companies, for example when buying other companies or going public on the stock exchange.

In the worldwide **financial crisis** of 2008, UBS lost a great deal of money through risky deals in the USA. To stop the bank from collapsing, the Confederation and the **Swiss National Bank** helped. The Confederation gave UBS six billion francs, which it later got back with a profit. Afterwards the rules for large banks became stricter.

**Credit Suisse** was founded in 1856 by Alfred Escher as the Schweizerische Kreditanstalt. After many scandals and losses, customers withdrew a great deal of money in a short time in March 2023. On 19 March 2023 it was announced that UBS would take over Credit Suisse, supported by the Confederation and the National Bank. With this, one of the oldest banks in Switzerland disappeared.

Today UBS is much bigger than the entire Swiss economy in a year. That is why it is considered **systemically important**, because its collapse would harm the whole country. Politicians and authorities are therefore discussing how much capital of its own the bank must have. The aim is that the state should never again have to rescue a big bank.

begriffe.erklaerung: When two companies join together to form a single one.
Investing and looking after money for customers.
A time when banks and stock exchanges have big problems.
A country’s central bank, which looks after money and its stability.

gewusst: After the takeover of Credit Suisse, UBS’s balance sheet is about twice as large as Switzerland’s annual economic output.

teile.einleitung: Threema is a messenger app from Switzerland that you can use to send messages, pictures and voice messages. What is special is that Threema puts great emphasis on data protection, and you do not need a phone number to sign up. All messages are end-to-end encrypted, so that only the sender and the recipient can read them.
wichtigste: Threema is a Swiss messenger for smartphones and computers.
You do not need a phone number to sign up.
End-to-end encryption means that only the sender and the recipient can read the message.
Threema came onto the market in 2012.
The company is based in Pfäffikon in the canton of Schwyz.
Threema’s servers are in Switzerland.
The app costs a small one-off amount instead of earning money from advertising.

abschnitte.text: Threema is a **messenger**, similar to WhatsApp or Signal. You can use it to chat, make calls, form groups and send files. The name contains the abbreviation **EEEMA** for “End-to-End Encrypting Messaging App”. Threema was developed by the Swiss computer scientist Manuel Kasper, and the app appeared in December 2012.

With **end-to-end encryption**, a message is turned into an unreadable code on your own phone. Only on the recipient’s phone is it made readable again. For this, each device has a secret **key** that never leaves the phone. That is why even the company Threema cannot read the messages.

Instead of a phone number, each person gets a random **Threema ID** of eight characters. So you can use the app without giving a number or an email address. You can verify contacts by scanning a **QR code**. This way you know for sure that you are writing to the right person.

Threema has several million users, mainly in Switzerland, Germany and Austria. Many companies and authorities use the **Threema Work** version. The Swiss Army also recommends Threema to its members for official messages. For schools there is a separate version called Threema Education.

Even in a secure messenger, you should only send pictures that you would also show other people. Once something has been sent, the recipient can forward it or save it with a **screenshot**. Never write to strangers who ask for personal details or photos. If you get unpleasant messages, it helps to talk to your parents or teachers.

begriffe.erklaerung: An app you can use to send messages to other people.
Turning a message into a secret code that only authorised people can read.
Protecting personal information from access by others.
The program code is public, and anyone can check it.

gewusst: Since 2020 the code of the Threema apps has been public, so that experts can check it for security gaps.
Threema stores messages on the server only until they have been delivered.
Because Threema does not need a phone number, you can also use it on a tablet without a SIM card.

teile.einleitung: The Zurich Insurance Group is one of the largest insurance companies in the world and has its headquarters in the city of Zurich. It all began in 1872 with insurance for goods transported on ships and wagons. Today Zurich protects millions of people and companies against damage of all kinds.
wichtigste: Zurich was founded in Zurich in 1872.
At the beginning it offered transport insurance.
Anyone who is insured pays the insurance company a premium regularly.
Today Zurich insures, for example, cars, houses, health and companies.
The group has about 55,000 employees worldwide (as of around 2024).
Zurich shares are traded on the Swiss stock exchange SIX.
Since 2012 the company has been called Zurich Insurance Group.

abschnitte.text: The company was founded in **1872** under the name “Versicherungs-Verein” (Insurance Association) and started work on 1 May 1873. At first it insured goods transported by ship, rail or wagon. If something was broken or lost on the way, the insurance paid for the damage. Such **transport insurance** was important at the time, because trade between countries was growing strongly.

abschnitte.titel: From small association to global group
abschnitte.text: As early as 1875 the company also started **accident insurance** and was now called Transport- und Unfall-Versicherungs-AG “Zürich”. From 1894 it concentrated on accident and liability insurance. Later many more countries were added. In 1998 Zurich took over the American insurer Farmers, which is very well known in the USA. Since 2012 the group has been called **Zurich Insurance Group**.

Many people regularly pay a small amount, the **premium**, into a common pot. If one of them suffers a large loss, for example a car accident or a fire, the insurance pays from this pot. This way nobody has to bear an expensive loss alone. The principle is called **solidarity**: many people together help a few.

The headquarters is at Mythenquai in Zurich, right on Lake Zurich. Zurich operates in a great many countries on all continents. It offers insurance for private individuals, for example for cars, household contents or travel, and also for large companies. There are also life insurance and retirement products. The head of the group since 2016 has been **Mario Greco**.

Zurich is one of the most valuable companies in Switzerland and is included in the **SMI** stock market index. It offers many jobs and apprenticeships in Switzerland. Switzerland is an important location for insurance; besides Zurich there are also, for example, Swiss Re and Die Mobiliar. Insurance companies also pay taxes and are therefore important for the country’s economy.

gewusst: Zurich was originally founded as a reinsurer, that is, as insurance for other insurance companies.
The blue Z in Zurich’s logo is known in many countries of the world.
The company is older than the telephone, which was only invented a few years after it was founded.
